questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The dimensions of gravitational constant are
questions.solution: From the formula $G=\frac{F R^2}{m_1 m_2}\begin{aligned} & G=\frac{\text { Dimensions of dimensions of force } F \times \text { dimension of }(R)^2}{\text { dimensions of mass } M \times \text { dimension of mass } M} \end{aligned}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right]\left[\mathrm{L}^2\right]}{[\mathrm{M}][\mathrm{M}]}=\left[\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^3 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone is thrown with an initial speed of $4.9 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ from a bridge in vertically upward direction. It falls down in water after 2 sec . The height of bridge is
questions.solution:
Here: Initial velocity $u=-4.9 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ (- ve is due to vertically upward motion)
Total time $t=2 \mathrm{sec}$
The height of the bridge is given by
$s=u t+\frac{1}{2} g t^2\begin{aligned} & =-4.9 \times 2+\frac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times(2)^2 \\ & =-9.8+19.6=9.8 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The earth of mass $=6 \times 10^{24} \mathrm{~kg}$ revolves around the sun with an angular velocity of $2 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ in a circular orbit of radius $1.5 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~km}$. The force exerted by the sun on earth is :
questions.solution:
Here: Mass of earth $M_e=6 \times 10^{24} \mathrm{~kg}$
Angular velocity of earth $\omega=2 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
Radius of circular orbit
$\begin{aligned}R & =1.5 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~km} \\& =1.5 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$
Force exerted on the earth by the sun is given by
$\begin{aligned}F & =M_e R \omega^2 \\& =6 \times 10^{24} \times 1.5 \times 10^{11} \times\left(2 \times 10^{-7}\right)^2 \\& =36 \times 10^{21} \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$

The work done will be:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The work done in pulling up a block of wood weighing 2 kN for a length of 10 m on a smooth plane inclined at an angle of $15^{\circ}$ with the horizontal is
questions.solution: Here : Weight of block $w=2 \mathrm{kN}$, Distance $d=10 \mathrm{~m}$ Angle of inclination on the plane $\alpha=15^{\circ}$ The block will be pulled up on a smooth plane Hence, force of resistance due to inclination $\begin{aligned} F & =w \sin \alpha=2 \times 10^3 \sin 15^{\circ} \\ & =2 \times 10^3 \times 0.2588 \\ & =0.5176 \mathrm{kN}\end{aligned}$ Now work done, $\begin{aligned}W=F d & =0.5176 \times 10^3 \times 10 \\& =5.17 \mathrm{kJ}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ moving with velocity $v$ collides with a stationary particle of mass $2 m$. The speed of the system, will be
questions.solution:
According to conservation of momentum
$\begin{gathered}m_1 v_1+m_2 v_2=\left(m_1+m_2\right) v^{\prime} \\
m v+2 m \times 0=(m+2 m) v^{\prime}\end{gathered}$
So,
$v^{\prime}=\frac{v}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.q: A ball of mass 10 g moving with acceleration of $20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ is hit by a force which acts on it for 0.1 sec . The impulsive force is
questions.solution:
Here: Mass of the ball $m=150 \mathrm{~g}\begin{aligned}& \text {time }=0.15 \mathrm{~kg} \\& \text {Acceleration of the ball }=20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 \\& \mathrm{dt} = 0.1 \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$
Force, $\quad F=m a=0.15 \times 20=3 \mathrm{~N}$
Now impulsive force
$=F \times d t=3 \times 0.1=0.3 \mathrm{Ns}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the heat of 110 J is added to a gaseous system, whose internal energy is 40 J , then the amount of external work done is
questions.solution:
Heat added to the system $\Delta Q=110 \mathrm{~J}$
Internal energy $\Delta u=40 \mathrm{~J}$
External work done is given by
$\Delta W=\Delta Q-\Delta u=110-40=70 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Amount of work which can be obtained from $200$ cal heat, will be
questions.solution:
Amount of work done is given by
$W=200 \mathrm{cal}=200 \times 4.2 \mathrm{~J}=840 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cylinder contains 10 kg of gas at pressure of $10^7 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2$. The quantity of gas taken out of the cylinder, if final pressure is $2.5 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2$ will be (temperature of gas is constant)
questions.solution:
Intital mass of the gas $m_1=10 \mathrm{~kg}$
Initial pressure $P_1=10 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2$
Final pressure $P_2=2.5 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2$
According to kinetic theory of gases
$P V=\frac{1}{3} m c^{-2}$
or $\quad P \propto m$
Hence, $\quad \frac{P_1}{P_2}=\frac{m_1}{m_2}$
or $\quad \frac{10^7}{2.5 \times 10^6}=\frac{10}{m_2}$
or $\quad m_2=2.5 \mathrm{~kg}$
Hence, quantity of gas taken out from the cylinder is $10-2.5=7.5 \mathrm{~kg}$

questions.q: The kinetic energy of one molecule of a gas at normal temperature and pressure will be $(k=8.31 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mole} \mathrm{K})$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The spring extends by $x$ on loading, then energy stored by the spring is (if $T$ is the tension in spring and $k$ is spring constant)
questions.solution:
The energy stored in the spring is
$E=\frac{1}{2} k x^2 \quad \ldots$ (i)
and expansion in the spring is
$x=\frac{T}{k}  \quad \ldots$ (ii)
From equations (i) and (ii), we get
$E=\frac{1}{2} k \frac{T^2}{k^2}=\frac{1}{2} \frac{T^2}{k}=\frac{T^2}{2 k}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A resonance air column of length 40 cm resonates with a tuning fork of frequency 450 Hz . Ignoring end correction, the velocity of sound in air will be
questions.solution:
Here : Length of column $=40 \mathrm{~cm}=0.4 \mathrm{~m}$
Frequency of tuning fork $=450 \mathrm{~Hz}$
Using the formula $n=\frac{v}{4 l}$ or
$\begin{aligned}v & =450 \times 4 \times 0.4 \\& =720 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If vibration of string is to be two times, then tension in the string must be made
questions.solution:
Here: Initial vibration $n_1=n$, final vibration $n_2=2 n$
Initial tension $T_1=T$
Vibration of frequency of string
$n=\frac{1}{2 l} \sqrt{\frac{T}{m}}\Rightarrow \quad n \propto \sqrt{T}$
Hence,
$\frac{n_1}{n_2}=\sqrt{\frac{T_1}{T_2}}$
or $\frac{T_1}{T_2}=\left(\frac{n_1}{n_2}\right)^2=\left(\frac{n}{2 n}\right)^2=\frac{1}{4}$
or $T_2=4 T_1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A siren emitting sound of frequency 500 Hz is going away from a stationary listener with a speed of $50 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, the frequency of sound heard directly from the siren is
questions.solution:
Here: Frequency of siren $=500 \mathrm{~Hz}$
The speed of siren $v_s=50 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
Using Doppler's principle
$n^{\prime}=\frac{v}{v+v_s} n$
or $\quad n^{\prime}=\left(\frac{330}{330+50}\right) \times 500$
or $\quad n^{\prime}=\frac{330 \times 500}{380} = 434.2 \mathrm{~Hz}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charged particle is suspended in equilibrium in a uniform vertical electric field of intensity $20000 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{m}$. If mass of the particle is $9.6 \times 10^{-16} \mathrm{~kg}$, the charge on it and excess number of electrons on the-particle respectively are $\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$
questions.solution:
Charge on the particle is given by
$\begin{aligned}q E & =m g \text { or } q=\frac{m g}{E} \\& =\frac{9.6 \times 10^{-16} \times 10}{20000}=4.8 \times 10^{-19}
\end{aligned}$
When there is an excess of $n$ electrons on the particle, then
$q=n e$
So,
$n=\frac{q}{e}=\frac{4.8 \times 10^{-19}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}}=3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The ratio of electrostatic and gravitational forces acting between electron and proton separated by a distance $5 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{~m}$, will be
(Charge on electron $=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$, mass of electron $=9.1 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}$, mass of proton $=1.6 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}$, $\left.G=6.7 \times 10^{-11} \quad \mathrm{Nm}^2 / \mathrm{kg}^2\right)$
questions.solution:
Gravitational force $F=\frac{G M_1 M_2}{r^2}F_G=\frac{6.7 \times 10^{-11} \times 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-27}}{\left(5 \times 10^{-11}\right)^2}=3.9 \times 10^{-47} \mathrm{~N}$
Electrostatic force $F_E=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}F_e=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}{\left(5 \times 10^{-11}\right)^2}=9.22 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~N}\therefore \quad \frac{\text { Electrostatic force }}{\text { Gravitational force }}=\frac{F_E}{F_G}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{9.22 \times 10^{-8}}{3.9 \times 10^{-47}} \\ & =2.36 \times 10^{39}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The capacity of an air condenser is 2.0 $\mu \mathrm{F}$. If a medium is placed between its plates, the capacity becomes $12 \mu \mathrm{F}$. The dielectric constant of the medium will be
questions.solution:
Dielectric constant of medium
$K=\frac{\text { capacity of condenser with medium }}{\text { capacity of condenser without medium }}=\frac{12}{2.0}=6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Taking the earth to be a spherical conductor of diameter $12.8 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~km}$. Its capacity will be
questions.solution:
Here : Diameter of earth
$\begin{aligned} & =12.8 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~km} \\
\text {So, radius } R & =\frac{12.8}{2} \times 10^3 \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =6.4 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~km}=6.4 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m} \\ \text { Capacity } C & =4 \pi \varepsilon_0 R =\frac{1}{9 \times 10^9} \times 6.4 \times 10^6 \\ & =711 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~F}=711 \mu \mathrm{F}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two equal resistances $R$ are joined with voltage source $V$ in (i) series (ii) parallel, the ratio of electrical power consumed in two cases wll be
questions.solution:
(i) In series: total resistance $=R+R=2 R$
Power consumed $P_1=\frac{V^2}{2 R} \quad \ldots$ (i)
(ii) In parallel : potential difference across each resistance will be $V$
So, power consumed in each resistance is
$P=\frac{V^2}{R}$
So total power consumed in two resistance is
$P_2=\frac{V^2}{R}+\frac{V^2}{R}=\frac{2 V^2}{R}$ \quad \ldots$ (ii)
$\begin{array}{r}\text { Hence, required ratio }=\frac{P_1}{P_2} \\ =\frac{V^2 \times R}{2 R \times 2 V^2}=\frac{1}{4}\end{array}

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resistance of a galvanometer is $50 \Omega$. When 0.01 A current flows in it, full scale deflection is obtained in galvanometer, the resistance of shunt connected to convert galvanometer into an ammeter of range 5 A , will be
questions.solution:
Here: $I_g=0.01 \mathrm{~A}, G=50 \Omega$
To convert the galvanometer in to an ammeter of range 5 A , a low resistance is to be connected in parallel with coil of galvanometer.
$S=\frac{i g \times G}{i-i_g}=\frac{0.01 \times 50}{5-0.01}=\frac{0.5}{4.99}=0.1 \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a resistance of $9 \Omega$ is connected at the ends of a battery, its potential difference decreases from 40 V to 30 V. The internal resistance of the battery is
questions.solution:
$E=40 \mathrm{~V}, V=30 \mathrm{~V}, R=9 \Omega$
Internal resistance
$r=\left(\frac{E}{V}-1\right) R=\left(\frac{40}{30}-1\right) 9=\frac{1}{3} \times 9=3 \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The equilvalent resistance and potential difference between $A$ and $B$ for the circuit respectively are
questions.solution:
The equivalent resistance between $A$ and $B$ is
$\frac{1}{R^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{2}{3}$
or $\quad R^{\prime}=\frac{3}{2}=1.5 \Omega$
Now the equivalent resistance between $A$ and $B$ is
$R^{\prime \prime}=1.5+2.5=4 \Omega$
Now by Ohm's law, potential difference between $A$ and $B$ is given by
$\begin{aligned} V_A-V_B & =i R=2 \times 4.0 \\ & =8 \mathrm{volt}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire of resistance $R$ is divided in n equal parts, then these parts are joined in parallel, the equivalent resistance of the combination will be
questions.solution:
Resistance of one part $\frac{R}{n}$
Now equivalent resistance of $n$ parts each of resistance $\frac{R}{n}$ in parallel is given by
$R^{\prime}=\frac{R / n}{n}=\frac{R}{n^2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A proton enters a magnetic field of intensity $1.5 \mathrm{~Wb} / \mathrm{m}^2$ with a velocity $2 \times 10^7 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ in a direction at an angle $30^{\circ}$ with the field. The force on the proton will be (charge on proton is $1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$ )
questions.solution:
Here: $q=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}, B=1.5 \mathrm{~Wb} / \mathrm{m}^2$,
$v=2 \times 10^7 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, \theta=30^{\circ}$ or $\sin 30^{\circ}=\frac{1}{2}$
Force on proton is given by
$F=q v B \sin \theta\begin{aligned} & =1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 2 \times 10^7 \times 1.5 \times \frac{1}{2} \\ & =2.4 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $20$ ampere current is flowing in a long straight wire. The intensity of magnetic field at a distance $10$ cm from the wire will be
questions.solution:
Here: $i=20 \mathrm{~A}, r=10 \mathrm{~cm}=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$
Intensity of magnetic field produced due to straight current carrying wire is
$B=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \times \frac{2 i}{r}\begin{aligned} & =10^{-7} \times \frac{2 \times 20}{0.1} \\ & =4 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~Wb} / \mathrm{m}^2\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular coil of mean radius of 7 cm and having 4000 turns is rotated at the rate of 1800 revolutions per minute in the earth's magnetic field $(B=0.5$ gauss), the emf induced in coil will be
questions.solution:
Here: $n=4000, B=0.5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~Wb} / \mathrm{m}^2$
Rate of rotation of coil $=1800 \mathrm{rev} / \mathrm{min}=\frac{1800}{60}=30 \mathrm{rev} / \mathrm{sec}\begin{aligned} & \omega=2 \pi f=2 \pi \times 30=60 \pi \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}, \\ & r=7 \mathrm{~cm}=0.07 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$
Now area of coil
$A=\pi r^2=\pi \times(0.07)^2=49 \pi \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2$
Now the maximum energy induced is
$\begin{aligned}e & =B A n \omega \\& =0.5 \times 10^{-4} \times 49 \pi \times 10^{-4} \times 4000 \times 60 \pi \\& =0.58 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the current 3 A flowing in the primary coil is made zero in 0.1 sec, the emf induced in the secondary coil is 1.5 volt. The mutual inductance between the coils is
questions.solution:
Here: $e=1.5$ volt
$\Delta i=0-3=-3 \mathrm{~A}, \Delta t=0.1 \mathrm{sec}$
Now the emf induced in secondary coil
$e=\frac{M \Delta i}{\Delta t} \quad$ (numerically)
or $\quad 1.5=\frac{M \times 3}{0.1}$
or $\quad M=\frac{1.5 \times 0.1}{3}=0.05 \mathrm{H}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transmitting station transmits radiowaves of wavelength 360 m . Calculate the inductance of coil required with a condenser of capacity $1.20 \mu \mathrm{F}$ in the resonant circuit to receive them
questions.solution:
The frequency of radiowaves (speed $c=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ ) transmitted
$f=\frac{c}{\lambda}=\frac{3 \times 10^8}{360}=8.3 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~Hz}$
Frequency of series resonant circuit
$\begin{aligned}f & =\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{L C}} \\\text { or } \quad L & =\frac{1}{(2 \pi f)^2 C}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{\left(2 \times 3.14 \times 8.3 \times 10^5\right)^2 \times 1.20 \times 10^{-6}} \\ & =3.07 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{H}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The peak value of alternating current is $5 \sqrt{2}$ ampere. The mean square value of current will be
questions.solution:
Here: $I_0=5 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~A}$
Root mean square value of current
$I_{\mathrm{rms}}=\frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}=5 \mathrm{~A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A lamp in which 10 amp current can flow at 15 V, is connected with an alternating source of potential 220 V. The frequency of source is 50 Hz. The inductance of choke coil required to light the bulb is
questions.solution:
The resistance of lamp
$R=\frac{V}{I}=\frac{15}{10}=1.5 \Omega$
The impedance of circuit
$Z=\frac{V}{I}=\frac{220}{10}=22 \mathrm{ohm}$
Again impedance $Z=\sqrt{R^2+\omega^2 L^2}$
or $\quad 22=\sqrt{(1.5)^2+(2 \times \pi \times 50)^2 L^2}$
or $\quad(22)^2=(1.5)^2+4 \pi^2 \times 50^2 \times L^2$
or $\quad L=0.07$ Henry

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 20 kV potential is applied across X-ray tube, the minimum wavelength of X-ray emitted will be
questions.solution:
From relation, $\frac{h c}{\lambda_{\min }}=e V$ or $\quad \lambda_{\min }=\frac{h c}{e V}$
or $\begin{aligned} \lambda_{\min } & =\frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 20 \times 10^3} \\ & =0.62 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~m}=0.62 Å\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student can distinctly see the object upto a distance 15 cm. He wants to see the black board at a distance of 3 m. Focal length and power of lens used respectively will be :
questions.solution:
The student should use a lens which forms image at distance of 15 cm of the object placed at 3 m i.e., object distance $u=-3 \mathrm{~m}=-300 \mathrm{~cm}$, image distance $v=-15 \mathrm{~cm}$
From lens formula $\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}$ 
we get $\quad \frac{1}{-15}-\frac{1}{-300}=\frac{1}{f}$
or $\quad \frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{300}-\frac{1}{15}=-\frac{19}{300}$
or $\quad f=\frac{-300}{19}=-15.8 \mathrm{~cm} \quad$ (concave lens)
Now power of the lens is
$P=\frac{100}{f(\mathrm{~cm})}=\frac{100}{-15.8}=-6.33 \mathrm{D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A this glass prism $(\mu=1.5)$ in the position of minimum deviation deviates the monochromatic light ray by $10^{\circ}$, the refracting angle of prism is
questions.solution:
Given : $\delta_m=10^{\circ}, \mu=1.5$
For a thin prism of minimum deviation
$\delta_m=(\mu-1) \mathrm{A}10^{\circ}=(1.5-1) \mathrm{A}$ or $A=\frac{10}{0.5}=20^{\circ}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two thin lenses of powers 12 D and -2 D respectively are placed in contact, the power, focal length and nature respectively will be
questions.solution:
Given: $P_1=12 \mathrm{D}, P_2=-2 \mathrm{D}$
Power of combination
$P=P_1+P_2=12-2=10 \mathrm{D}$
Focal length $f=\frac{1}{P}=\frac{1}{10} \mathrm{~m}=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$
The combined lens will be convex (convergent)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The half life of a radioactive substance is 3.6 days. How much of 20 mg of this radioactive substance will remain after 36 days?
questions.solution:
Half life $T_{1 / 2}=3.6$ days
Initial quantity $N_0=20 \mathrm{mg}$
Total time $=36$ days
The number of half lives
$n=\frac{t}{T_{1 / 2}}=\frac{36}{3.6}=10$
Hence, mass of radioactive substance left after 10 half lives
$N=N_0 \times\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n=20 \times \frac{1}{1024}=0.019 \mathrm{mg}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The energy in MeV is released due to transformation of 1 kg mass completely into energy, is $\left(c=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\right)$
questions.solution:
According to Einstein's mass energy equivalence
$E=m c^2=1 \times\left(3 \times 10^8\right)^2=9 \times 10^{16} \mathrm{~J}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{9 \times 10^{16}}{1.6 \times 10^{-13}} \mathrm{MeV} \\ & \quad \text { (since } 1 \mathrm{MeV}=1.6 \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~J} \text { ) }\end{aligned}=5.625 \times 10^{29} \mathrm{MeV}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In junction diode, the holes are because of
questions.solution: In semiconductor, when an electron leaves its place, a positive charge is left behind and it is known as hole. Hence, holes are created becauase of missing electrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the $C B$ mode of a transistor, when the collector voltage is changed by 0.5 volt, the collector current changes by 0.05 mA . The output resistance will be
questions.solution:
Here:
$\begin{aligned}& \Delta V_c=0.5 \mathrm{volt}, \\
& \Delta I_c=0.05 \mathrm{~mA}=0.05 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~A} \end{aligned}$
Output resistance is given by
$\begin{aligned} R_{\text {out }} & =\frac{\Delta V_c}{\Delta I_c} \\ & =\frac{0.5}{0.05 \times 10^{-3}}=10^4 \Omega=10 \mathrm{~K} \Omega\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The kinetic energy of an electron is 5 eV . Calculate the de-Broglie wavelength associated with it $\left(h=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}\right.$, $m_e=9.1 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}$ )
questions.solution:
Wavelength associated with an electron
$\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m E}}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2 \times 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times 5 \times 1.6 \times 10^{19}}} \\ & =5.47 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~m}=5.47 Å\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The significant figures in $1.0024,1.240$ and 0.0020 are respectively
questions.solution: In 1.0024 , all figures are significant. In 1.240 ,the significant figures are four (zero tells about precision). Zero before a number are not significant, hence 0.0020 has only two significant numbers (2 and 0 after 2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Volume of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ obtained from complete decomposition of $20 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{CaCO}_3$ at STP is
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{r}\because 100 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{CaCO}_3, \text { on decomposition, gives } =22.4 \text { litre } \mathrm{CO}_2 \text { at STP }\end{array} $\therefore 20 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{CaCO}_3$, on decomposition, will give $=\frac{22.4 \times 20}{100}=4.48 \text { litre } \mathrm{CO}_2 \text { at STP }

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following, is not a unit of pressure?
questions.solution:
Newton is not the unit of pressure. It is the unit of force. Atmosphere, torr and pascal $(P a)$ are the units of pressure.
$\begin{aligned} & 1 \text { atm. }=1.01 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~Pa} \\ & 1 \text { torr }=133.3 \mathrm{~Pa}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A golf-ball weigh 40.0 g . If it is moving with a velocity of $20.0 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$, it's de-Broglie wavelength is
questions.solution:
From de-Broglie equation,
$\lambda=\frac{h}{m v}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \lambda & =\frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{j} . \mathrm{s}}{40 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~kg} \times 20.0 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}} \\ & =8.28 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =8.28 \times 10^{-34} \times 10^9 \mathrm{~nm} \\ & =8.28 \times 10^{-25} \mathrm{~nm}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which is the shortest wavelength line in the Lyman series of the hydrogen spectrum?
$\text { ( } R=1.097 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~nm}^{-1} \text { ) }$
questions.solution:
For Lyman series, $\frac{1}{\lambda}=R\left(\frac{1}{(1)^2}-\frac{1}{n^2}\right)$ hence, for $\lambda$ to be smallest, $n$ should be greatest (i.e., $\infty$ )
$\therefore \quad \frac{1}{\lambda_{\min }}=1.097 \times 10^{-2}\left(1-\frac{1}{\infty^2}\right)\begin{aligned} & =1.097 \times 10^{-2} \\ \text { or } \quad \lambda_{\min } & =\frac{1}{1.097 \times 10^{-2}}=91.16 \mathrm{~nm}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ions, has smallest size?
questions.solution: $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}, \mathrm{Cl}^{-}, \mathrm{S}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{K}^{+}$are isoelctronic species. In isoelectronic ions, size decrease with increasing nuclear charge. Hence, $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ ion is the smallest among these.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following order of ionisation energy is correct?
questions.solution: Ionisation energy generally increase in a period from left to right. But due to comparatively stabler configuration of Be $\left(1 s^2, 2 s^2\right)$, it has more ionisation energy than Boron $\left(1 s^2, 2 s^2, 2 p^1\right)$. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The enthalpies of all elements in their standard states are

Oxygen $\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)$ contains 2 unpaired electron, hence it is paramagnetic

questions.solution: $(l p s+\sigma-b p s=1+3=4)$ hence, hybridisation $=s p^3\mathrm{PCl}_3$ has $s p^3$ hybridisation but due to presence of one lone pair, it is pyramidal in geometry. (Inspite of being tetrahedral)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Lunar caustic is
questions.solution: $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ is also called lunar caustic as it leaves white scar on skin due to reduction to silver by skin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following forms molecular solid?
questions.solution: $\mathrm{SO}_2$, on cooling comes into solid form, which is due to weak van der Waal's forces. Such type of solids are called molecular solids. All other are covalent solids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:

$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}^{\prime}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{\mathrm{~K}}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The $K a$ of an acid is $3.2 \times 10^{-5}$. The degree of dissociation of the acid at concentration of 0.2 M is

From Ostwald's dilution law

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH of $10^{-8} \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NaOH}$ is
questions.solution:
For $10^{-8} \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NaOH}$,
$\left[\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right]=10^{-8}+10^{-7} \quad$ (from water)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxide that gives $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ on treatment with dilute acid is
questions.solution: Peroxides give hydrogen peroxide, on treatment with dilute acids. Hence, only sodium peroxide $\left(\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{O}_2\right)$ will give $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following elements, is a component of a compound essential for photosynthesis?
questions.solution: Magnesium is found in chlorophyll, the green pigment, essential for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following dissolves in hot conc. NaOH solution?
questions.solution:
Zinc is quite reactive metal. It dissolves in excess of hot NaOH to give sodium zincate.
$\mathrm{Zn}+2 \mathrm{NaOH} \longrightarrow \underset{\text { sodium zincate }}{\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{ZnO}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \uparrow}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following, is a mordant dye?
questions.solution: Mordant dyes are those dyes, which cannot be fixed directly on fabric but require some fixating agents (like Cr salts) e.g., Alizarin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of stability of carbocations, is :
questions.solution:
More the +I alkyl groups on electron deficient carbon, more stable will be the cabocation. Hence, $3^{\circ}$ carbocations are more stable.
The correct order is $3^{\circ}\gt2^{\circ}\gt1^{\circ}\gt\mathrm{CH}_3^+$

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.solution: Hence, correct IUPAC name is = bicyclo [2, 2, 0] hexane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The following compound can not exhibit
$\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH}) - \mathrm{COOH}$
questions.solution: The compound can show optical isomerism, geometrical isomerism and position isomerism. But it cannot exhibit metamerism as it has no functional group which is polyvalent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is obtained, when potassium succinate soluton is electrolysed?
questions.solution: This is an example of Kolbe's electrolysis. Ethylene is obtained on electrolysis of potassium succinate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Addition of a non-volatile solute causes lowering in vapour pressure of a solvent from 0.8 atm to 0.2 atm. What is the mole fraction of solvent?
questions.solution:
From Raoult's law, $\frac{P-P_s}{P}=$ mole fraction of solute $\left(x_A\right)\therefore \quad x_A=\frac{0.8-0.2}{0.8}=\frac{0.6}{0.8}=0.75$
Hence, mole-fraction of solvent
$=1-0.75=0.25$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two metals 'A' and 'B' have $\mathrm{E}_{\text {red }}^{\circ}$ value equal to 0.36 V and 1.23 V . What will be the correct cell equation?
questions.solution:
From $E_{\text {red }}^{\circ}$. values, it is clear that $A$ is more electropositive than $B$ (as it has lesser $E^{\circ}{ }_{\text {red }}$ ), hence it can replace $B$ from its salt solution and act as anode in galvanic cell. Hence, correct cell equation will be:
$A+B^{2+} \longrightarrow A^{2+}+B$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a reaction, the half-life is independent of initial concentration. What is the order of that reaction?
questions.solution:
For an $n^{\text {th }}$ order reaction,
$t_{1 / 2} \propto \frac{1}{C^{n-1}} \quad(C=\text { initial conc. })$
Hence, for Ist order reaction $(n=1)$, we have
$t_{1 / 2} \propto \frac{1}{C^{1-1}}\therefore \quad t_{1 / 2} \propto C^0$
Thus half life of Ist order reaction is independent of the initial concentration of reactant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statement is not correct?
options: Adsorption energy for chemical adsorption is generally greater than that of physical adsorption
Physical adsorption is due to van der Waal forces
Physical adsorption decreases at high temperature and low pressure
questions.solution: Physical adsorption is due to van der Waal's forces which are weak forces, hence this type of adsorption is reversible and not irreversible. All other statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Solvent loving colloids are known as
questions.solution: Solvent loving colloids are called lyophilic colloids. These are natural, reversible colloids which easily form colloidal solution e.g., albumin, gelatin, gum-arabic etc

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: Bauxite is an ore of
questions.solution: Bauxite $\left(\mathrm{Al} 203 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 0\right)$ is the most important ore of aluminium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following acids is monobasic?
questions.solution: $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_2$ (hypophosphorus acid) is a monobasic acid. It gives only one type of salt e.g., $\mathrm{NaH}_2 \mathrm{PO}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Yellow phosphorus is kept in
questions.solution: Phosphorus (white or yellow) is kept preserved in water as it catches fire in air at normal temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following turns potassium dichromate paper green?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{SO}_2$ gas is a reducing agent, hence turns dichromate paper green due to formation of chromium sulphate. Sulphite radical $\left(\mathrm{SO}_3^{2-}\right)$ is identified by this:
$\mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7+3 \mathrm{SO}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \underset{\text { green }}{\mathrm{Cr}_2\left(\mathrm{SO}_4\right)_2} +\mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHCl}_2$, on hydrolysis, will give
questions.solution: gem dihalides, on hydrolysis, give carbonyl compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The compound which reacts faster with Lucas reagent is
questions.solution: Tertiary alcohols react faster with Lucas reagent. They give turbidity with Lucas reagent (cone. $\mathrm{HCl}+$ anhyd. $\mathrm{ZnCl}_2$ ) at once. Hence, 2-methyl propan-2-ol will react with Lucas reagent faster.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following has the maximum acidic strength ?
questions.solution: $o$-nitrobenzoic acid is the strongest acid among these. $-\mathrm{NO}_2$ group is a powerful electron withdrawing group and it has most effect when present at $o$-position. It is also known as o-effect. Due to its electron withdrawing nature electron density on H -atom in -COOH group becomes very less, hence it can be easily donated.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Enzymes are absent in
questions.solution: Virus is without necessary metabolic enzymes, hence, free virus are inert particles incapable of any vital activities and uses host machinery. Virus is regarded as obligate parasite and have characteristic of both living and non-livings.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The first phylogenetic system of plant classification was proposed by
questions.solution: The first phylogenetic system was proposed by Eichler who is famous for his work entittled "Bluthen Diagramme" published in two volumes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Black rust of wheat is a fungal disease caused by
questions.solution: Puccinia graminis tritici belongs to class Basidiomycetes. It causes black rust of wheat.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: 'Reindeer moss' is common name for
questions.solution: The bitter substance present in lichens are removed before being used as fodder. Lichens form favourite food for reindeers, cattles etc. Cladonia rangifera is the commonly used food for reindeer in tundra regions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Yeast belongs to which class?
questions.solution: The yeast (Saccharomyces) is a saprophytic fungus which belongs to class Ascomycetes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mannitol is reserve food in
questions.solution: Class Phaeophyceae includes brown algae Brown algae are marine plants. Chief pigments found in the members of this class are chloropyll $a$ and $c$, $\beta$-carotene, violaxanthin, fucoxanthin, lutein, diatoxanthin. Reserve food is laminarin, mannitol and oils.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plants growing on sand and gravel are called
questions.solution: Psammophytes grow in sand and gravel, eremophytes grow in desert and gravel, psilophytes grow in savanna and oxylophytes grow on acidic soil.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The amphibians of plant kingdom are
questions.solution: In bryophytes water is essential for fertilization. It provides a medium of transport for antherozoids to reach archegonia. Hence, they are called amphibians of plant kingdom.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Chlorophyceae the mode of sexual reproduction is
questions.solution: In isogamy, gametes are morphologically and physiologically same, in anisogamy gametes are morphologically different but physiologically same and in oogamy, gametes are both morphologically and physiologically different e.g., Ulothrix and Spirogyra members of Chlorophyceae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Algal zone is present in
questions.solution: The cortex in coralloid roots of Cycas is divided into inner and outer regions by algal zone. The cells of this zone contain endophytic algal forms particularly Anabaena cycadeae and Nostoc punctiforme.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Heterospory is the production of
questions.solution: In some pteridophytes two types of spores are formed which differ significantly in their size and also in function. This phenomenon is called heterospory e.g., Selaginella and Marsilea etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The scientist, who described the birds as glorified reptiles, was
questions.solution: Huxley stated that birds are glorified reptiles. The missing link Archaeopteryx is a fossil lizard bird. It was founded by Andreas Wagner (1861) from upper Jurassic limestone rocks of Solenbofen in Bowaria, Germany.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is left when bath sponges dries up?
questions.solution: Euspongia is called bath spongia. The sponge are classified on the basis of skeleton which is made up of spongin fibere. After the bath sponge dries only the skeleton is left.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The inflorescence in Ocimum is :
questions.solution: Verticillaster consists of biparous cymes ending in uniparous scorpioid cymes on either side e.g. Ocimum and several members of family Labiatae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cellulose fibre is obtained from Gossypium _______.
questions.solution: Cotton is the seed surface fibre of Gossypium. Its processing involves ginning, bailing, picking, lapping, carding and twisting. It is used in textile industry.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Periderm includes :
options: cork cambium, cork and secondary cortex
questions.solution: Periderm formation occurs in the root and stems of dicots and gymnosperm in extra stelar region with the help of cork cambium. Periderm is external secondary protective tissue and compreses of cork, cork cambium and secondary cortex.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which type of enzyme is present in lysosome?
questions.solution: Lysosomes or suicidal bags are bounded by single unit membrane. It contains hydrolytic enzymes which help to digest the nucleic acids, proteins and polysaccharide etc. (i.e., extracellular material). It also helps in autolysis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Phospholipids are
questions.solution: The phospholipid is a bipolar molecule having long fatty acid called hydrophobic tail (water hating) or non-polar end. Another is hydrophillic (water loving) or polar end, hence, it is amphipathic in nature.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which type of DNA is found in bacteria?
questions.solution: Bacteria are prokaryotic in nature, in which typical chromosomes are lacking. DNA is circular and naked as it is not surrounded by his tones (basic proteins).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is a day neutral plant?
questions.solution: Day neutral plants do not need a specific photoperiod to produce flowers. They are also called intermediates or photoneutrals. Their photoperiod varies from a few hours to 24 hours of uninterrupted light e.g. tomato, cucumber, sunflower, Helianthus annuus, maize and cotton etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is an antigibberellin?
questions.solution: The ABA inhibits gibberellin induced growth activities on account of this antagonistic behaviour, it is also called antigibberellin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The real forces responsible for the movement of water from one cell to another cell is mainly
questions.solution: The net force with which water is drawn into a cell is equal to difference of OP and TP, known as diffusion pressure deficit or suction pressure. DPD of pure water is maximum ( $\approx 1236 \mathrm{~atm}$ ) solvent moves from cell of low DPD to high DPD. DPD, or $\mathrm{SP}=\mathrm{OP}-\mathrm{TP}$.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The magnitude of root pressure ranges from:
questions.solution: The term root pressure was coined by Stephen Hales (1727). The evidences that support the existence of this phenomenon are bleeding and guttation. The magnitude of root pressure is $1-2 \mathrm{~atm}$ and very rarely 5 atm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The terminal electron acceptor during electron transport system is
questions.solution:
Oxygen is the terminal acceptor of electron in electron transport system, which in the presence of proton forms a water molecule
$\begin{gathered}\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2+2 e \longrightarrow \mathrm{O}^{2-} \\ 2 \mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{O}^{2-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\end{gathered}$

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Glycolysis occurs in
questions.solution: Glycolysis or Embden Myerhof Parna spathway takes place in cytoplasm. It is a common phase between aerobic and anaerobic respiration. The enzymes occur in cytosol.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following element plays an important role in nitrogen fixation?
questions.solution: Molybdenum is a component of nitrogenase and thus brings about fixation of gaseous nitrogen. It also act as enzyme activator of nitrate reductase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Hatch and Slack type plants $\mathrm{CO}_2$ acceptor is
questions.solution: In Hatch and Slack cycle $\mathrm{CO}_2$ acceptor is phosphoenol pyruvic acid and first product is oxaloacetic acid, (a $4-\mathrm{C}$ compound). Therefore it is popularly termed as $\mathrm{C}_4$ cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In CAM plants
options: stomata open in day and close at night
stomata remain open in day and night both
stomata remain closed in day and night both
stomata open at night and close in day
questions.solution: CAM is found in members of the family Crassulaceae (e.g., Kalanchoe), family Cactaceae (e.g., Opuntia, Cereus), and some members of Liliaceae, Orchidaceae, Bromeliaceae, Euphorbia sp. All CAM plants are not succulent and stomata open at night.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If the pollen tube enters the ovule through funiculus, the phenomenon is known as
questions.solution: In porogamy the pollen tube enters the ovule through micropyle, in chalazogamy pollen tube enters through chalaza and in mesogamy pollen tube enters through funiculus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is the most resistant material in pollen grain?
questions.solution: Sporopollenin is most resistant chemical substance in pollen grains wall.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Double fertilization means
options: fusion of nucleus of male gamete with the egg nucleus
fusion of sperm nucleus with secondary nucleus
fusion of one sperm nucleus with nucleus and fusion of other sperm nucleus with secondary nucleus
questions.solution: Double fertilization is the process the one sperm fuses with the egg while the other sperm fuses with the two polar nuclei. mien pollen tube enters ovule, it strikes one of the synergids and burst open to release the two male gametes which fuses with two different structures in the same female gametophyte. The fusion two polar nuclei forms endosperm. So, the correct answer is option D.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which genera endospores are formed for reproduction?
questions.solution: Some species of bacteria reproduce sexually with the help of endospores. Endospores are thick-walled spores, formed singly in a bacterial cell. These are commonly seen in the species of Bacillus and Clostridium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Spirogyra sometimes a ladder like structure is present due to :
questions.solution: Sexual reproduction in Spirogyra takes place by conjugation. Scalariform conjugation occurs between the cells belonging to different filaments. Hence, these species are heterothallic. Lateral conjugation is primitive than scalariform conjugation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The basic unit of chitin is
questions.solution: The chitin (= polyglycosamine) is an acetate of mucopolysaccharide called glycosamine which is formed by the combination of polysaccharide with small peptide molecules. The basic unit (monomer) of chitin is $N$-acetylglucosamine, monomers are joined by $1-4 \beta$ linkages.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Arachidonic acid is
questions.solution: olyunsaturated (i.e., have more than one double bond) and essential fatty acids. Essential fatty acids cannot be synthesised by the body of animal and has to be taken from outside to fulfil the body requirement. Linoleic acid and linolenic acid are also essential fatty acids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statement is correct about DDT ?
options: It is a biomagnifying biodegradable pollutant
It is non biomagnifying biodegradable pollutant
It is biomagnifying non biodegradable pollutant
questions.solution: DDT has been recently banned because it is non-biodegradable and biomagnifying pollutant. Biomagnification means the increase in amount of DDT in the body of organism along with the increase in trophic level. Hence, the amount of DDT in 1st trophic level will be minimum and in top consumer will be maximum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Agricultural chemicals include
questions.solution: As growth regulators control the growth of plants, pesticides control the pests and fertilizers enhance productivity of the soil, hence all of these are regarded as agricultural chemicals

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which is social foresting species?
questions.solution: Leucaena leucocephala is commonly known as subabool. It is a very fast growing leguminous plant and therefore is commonly used as social foresting species.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In terrestrial ecosystem such as forest, maximum energy is found in which trophic level?
questions.solution: In all ecosystem the maximum amount of energy is found in trophic level $1-r\mathrm{t}_1$ (i.e. the producers) which keeps on decreasing along the higher trophic level.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Third cleavage of frog's development is
questions.solution: First and second cleavage in frog are holoblastic, complete, equal, vertical, whereas third cleavage is holoblastic, complete, unequal, latitudinal or horizontal and near the animal pole. It results in the formation 8 cells of which three are black micromeres which have less or no yolk, so divide faster and 4 are colourless macromeres.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The epithelial lining in the alveoli of the frogs facing lung cavity is
questions.solution: Alveoli is highly vascularised with an internal lining of very thin squamous epithelium, which always remain moist by mucus. The epithelial cells at the linar most margins of septa facing lung cavity are columnar and ciliated.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is a transparent tissue?
questions.solution: Hyaline cartilage has a clear, homogenous, transparent bluish-green matrix. It gives glass like appearance. A few bundles of small white fibres are imbedded in the matrix. It is present in the end of limb bones (called hyaline caps).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In frog, the vertebra with an anterior convex surface (i.e., double convexties) is
questions.solution: The 9 th or sacral vertebra is acoelous and highly specialised the anterior face is convex for this give greater strength to them, it would be given if its anterior end are hollowed out the transverse process are stout and downwardly directed. The ileum of the pelvic girdle articulates with the transverse process of 9 th vertebra.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: RBC's are nucleated in
questions.solution: RBC in man is anucleated. Nucleated RBCs are found in camel and amphibians (e.g. frog). In frog, RBCs are typically flattened and more or less eliptical in shape but it appears biconvex when seen along its edge. They are filled with cytoplasm of faint straw colour and contains a definite round nucleus in centre.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is both exocrine and endocrine gland?
questions.solution: Pancreas are partially exocrine and partially endocrine glands.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Blood calcium level can be increased by the administration of
questions.solution: Blood calcium level is regulated by Parathormone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The true stomach in ruminants where most of digestion takes place is
questions.solution:
In ruminants (e.g., cow, goat and camel) the stomach is 4 chambered as follows
(1) Rumen (cellulose is digested)
(2) Reticulum (cellulose is digested)
(3) Omasum (absorb water)
(4) Abomasum (true stomach)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: At high altitude, RBC's of human blood will
questions.solution: At height above 8000 m from sea level, the partial pressure of $\mathrm{O}_2$ in air is decreased. As a result less haemoglobin is formed and the person suffers from dizziness, breathlessness etc. This is called mountain sickness. A continuous exposure to this height increases ventilation to about 3 to 7 times normal then there is significant increase in RBC count and haemoglobin content in blood and breathing becomes normal.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In which blood group antigens are absent?
questions.solution: Person with blood group 'O' has no antigen on his RBC but has both the antibodies (i.e., a and b) in his plasma. Whereas a person with blood group ' $A B$ ' has both antigens but no antibody. Due to this blood group ' O ' is universal donor and blood group ' $A B$ ' is universal acceptor.

questions.q: The first heart sound is produced when
options: bicuspid and tricuspid valve close quickly
questions.solution: During working of heart two sounds are produced lub and dub. First sound (i.e., lub) is produced when auriculoventricular (tricuspid and bicuspid) valves are closed or at the end of diastole. The second sound (i.e., dub) is produced when semilunar valves at the base of dorsal aorta are closed or at the end of systole.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Ventricles are related to
questions.solution: oth heart and brain. Mammalian heart is four chambered. The upper two chambers known as right and left auricle and the lower as right and left ventricles. In brain there are four ventricles. Ventricle Ist and II (lateral ventricles) are cavities of two cerebral hemispheres. IIIrd ventricle (diocoel) is cavity of diencephalon and IV ventricle (metacoel) is cavity of medulla oblongata.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is the part of mid brain of rabbit?
questions.solution: The dorsal part of mid brain (mesencephalon) is in the form of two pairs (i.e., four) of spherical optic lobes (corpora quadrigemina) located behind the pineal body optic lobes are reduced merely as reflex centres of visual and auditory.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Organ of Corti is found in
questions.solution: Organ of Corti are found in cochlear channel (internal ear) and are responsible for hearing. Ear is concerned both with hearing and balance, semicircular canals are responsible for balance when body is in motion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: ADH controls water permeability of
questions.solution: The vasopressin hormone, secreted by neurohypophysis of pituitary gland promotes the reabsorption of water from the distal convoluted tubules of nephrons, reducing excretion of water in urine (= diuresis). Hence, it is called antidiuretic Hormone (ADH). Its release in blood is controlled by an 'osmoregulatory centre" located in hypothalamus. Hyposecretion of ADH causes diabetes incipidus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following amino acids are present in ornithine cycle?
questions.solution: Ornithine cycle takes place in liver. The amino acid arginine and citrulline are formed during this cycle. Therefore it is referred as ornithine, arginine cycle and also Kreb-Henseleit cycle. The products of this cycle are urea and ornithine. The substances excreted through this cycle are $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{NH}_3$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The vital capacity of lungs is equal to
questions.solution:
The vital capacity is the maximum amount of air that can be expelled from lungs by forced exhalation after a forced inhalation. It is equal to the sum of tidal volume (TV), inspiratory reserve volume (IRV) and expiratory reserve volume (ERV).
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{VC} & =\mathrm{TV}+\mathrm{IRV}+\mathrm{ERV} \\ & =500+3000+1100 \\ & =4600 \mathrm{ml}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: CO is harmful to human being because
options: it competes $\mathrm{O}_2$ to combine with haemoglobin
questions.solution: Haemoglobin forms a stable compound with CO. The affinity of haemoglobin for CO is 200 times more than for $\mathrm{O}_2$ so even $0.1 \%$ CO blocks $50 \%$ haemoglobin of the body due to which oxygen carrying capacity of blood is decreased. This is called hypoxia.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Striped muscles are
questions.solution: Striped (striated or skeletal or voluntary) muscles are syncytial. Nuclei are spindle shaped, peripheral in position and lie near the sarcolemma. They are multi nucleate because each fibre is formed by the fusion of a number of embryonic stem cells (myoblasts), hence, regarded multicellular syncytial body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The joint of radio-ulna with the upper arm is
questions.solution: In hinge joint a condyle at the end of one bone fits in the depression of other bone in such a manner that the bone with condyle can swung like a loop on its hinge only in one direction e.g. leg elbow joint, ankle joint and knee joint etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following assists in the locomotion of the organism stated?
questions.solution: Hirudinaria belongs to class Hirudinea of phylum-Annelida. It has definite number of body segments $(26+7=33)$. It feeds on blood (sanguivorous) and has anticoagulant hirudin in its saliva. Hirudinaria have a posterior sucker for locomotion. Leech creep by looping and swim by undulations of body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Incomplete division of egg during cleavage is known as
questions.solution: In meroblastic cleavage, division occurs only in small amount of metabolically active cytoplasm, confined to the animal pole or peripheral region of egg. The yolk remains undivided. It is found in macrolecithal eggs. e.g. birds

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The immediate cause of induction of ovulation in female is the large plasma surge of
questions.solution: Ovulation takes place on 14th day of cycle, concentration of LH is highest on 14th day because it has to break the Graafian follicle so as to release the ovum later if the concentration of estrogen and progesterone decrease there is lose of internal lining of uterus and menstural bleeding start.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A nucleoside is
questions.solution: Base + sugar form a nucleoside and base + sugar + phosphate group combine together to give a nucleotide.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In split genes the coding sequences are called
questions.solution: Split genes were discovered by Phillip Sharp and Robert Richard. The part of DNA which express itself by making $m$ RNA is called exon. One exon is separated from other by inactive part of DNA called intron. This is called split DNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: DNA polymerase enzyme is required for synthesis of :
questions.solution: The enzyme needed for replication of DNA i.e. formation of DNA from DNA is DNA polymerase III. DNA replication is initiated by RNA primer which is later removed by DNA polymerase I.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A person who is trisomic for twenty first pair of chromosome suffers from
questions.solution: Down's syndrome $(45+\mathrm{XX}$ or $45+\mathrm{XY})$ is the case when there is one extra chromosome in 21st pair of autosome. It is also called trisomy 21 or trisomy-G. It is most common in children of over aged mothers (above 41 years). It is also called Mongolian syndrome.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A man of blood group 'A', marries a woman of blood group 'B', both of them are heterozygous for blood group, chances of their first child having blood group AB will be
questions.solution: Man Blood group Women Blood group There is $25 \%$ chances of first offspring having blood group AB.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: $2 n-1$ condition represent
questions.solution: When changes involve only a few chromosome say one or two and not the entire genome, the phenomenon is called aneuploidy. Monosomy is a case of aneuploidy, when there is loss of one chromosome from a pair of homologue.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Dinosaurs become extinct in
questions.solution: Dinosaurs become extinct in cretaceous period.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following is vestigeal organ of human?
questions.solution: Vestigeal organs are present in reduced form and are of no use to the animal in which they are present. Man has, 180 vestigeal organs. e.g., nictitating membrane, vermiform appendix, wisdom tooth, muscle of pinna and forhead, mammary glands in male etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Stanley Miller performed an experiment to prove the origin of life. They took gases $\mathrm{NH}_3$ and $\mathrm{H}_2$ along with
questions.solution: Stanley Miller using $\mathrm{CH}_4: \mathrm{NH}_3: \mathrm{H}_2$ gases in the ratio of $2: 2: 1$ and water vapours synthesised many simple organic compounds including amino acids, glycine, alanine and aspartic acid. According to him life originated from $\mathrm{NH}_3, \mathrm{CH}_4, \mathrm{H}_2$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The larvicidial fish used in biocontrol of mosquitoes
questions.solution: Gambusia is an exotic fish feeds on the larvae of mosquito. Now-a-days it is widely used to eradicate mosquito.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The infective stage of Plasmodium is
questions.solution: Infective stage of Plasmodium is a sporozoite inoculated into human blood by female Anopheles. Sporozoite are produced due to gamogony (sexual cycle in the stomach of mosquito) followed by sporogony (asexual cycle in the stomach wall of mosquito). Sporozoites are sickle or spindle-shaped.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Peyer's patches produce
questions.solution: Peyer's patches are found in ileum and made up of lymph nodes. These are aggregates of lymphocytes where B cells form a central follicle and are surrounded by T-cells and macrophages which help the T-cells to recognise Antigen Mucosa Associated Lymphoid Tissue (MALT) is made up of Peyer's patches.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Restriction enzymes are used in genetic engineering, because they
options: can cut DNA at specific base sequence
are nucleases that cut DNA at variable sites
questions.solution: Restriction enzyme are also known as molecular knifes or molecular scissors. They are isolated from bacteria. They recognize specific base sequence in DNA and cleave both strands of it

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.solution: Restriction enzyme recognises specific nucleotide sequences in DNA and then makes a double-stranded cleavage of DNA molecule. Restriction enzymes are called genetic scissors as they slice off genes and is recently being used in gene therapy technique. They are key tool of genetic engineering. Central dogma is related with protein synthesis. Okazaki fragments are found during DNA synthesis and RNA polymerase is used in synthesis of RNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Micro-organism which act as a vehicle for foreign gene transfer in higher plants:
questions.solution: The bacterium-Agrobacterium acts as a vehicle for transfer of DNA or genes from one organism to another organism because it infects all dicot plants.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The effect of intraspecific competition on niches is to make them
questions.solution: The intraspecific competition makes the size of niche smaller due to keen competition among the members.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The Orobanche plant is
questions.solution: Total root parasites have no chlorophyll. These are common on the roots of Cruciferae and Solanaceae e.g., Balanophora and Orobanche etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The part of earth in which life exist is known as ?
questions.solution: Biosphere is the part of earth where life exists.
